question: Can initialization scale and weight decay steer Transformers away from memorized composite mappings toward lower-complexity primitive rules that generalize to unseen combinations?

key_findings.claim: Author-reported phase diagram: progressively smaller parameter initialization and stronger weight decay move GPT-2 from poor generalization, through memorized pair-level mappings, to primitive-level compositional generalization.
key_findings.evidence: On a four-anchor arithmetic task, 14 of 16 anchor pairs are trained and (c,d)/(d,c) are held out. Across initialization exponent gamma and weight decay, the authors define Phase 1 as poor ID/OOD accuracy, Phase 2 as good ID but poor OOD, and Phase 3 as good ID/OOD. Three-seed heatmaps show the transition, though thresholds such as 90% ID, 50% OOD, and 70% commutativity are analyst-selected rather than theoretically derived.

key_findings.claim: Masking probes are consistent with pair memorization in Phase 2 and stepwise single-anchor computation in Phase 3, but they do not establish a unique causal circuit.
key_findings.evidence: After masking key-token information, output projections increasingly cluster by anchor-pair relationships. After masking the second anchor, Phase-3 outputs with the same first-step value g(x;a1) have high cosine similarity whereas Phase-2 outputs do not. Masking is imposed after attention softmax and changes the computation off-distribution; PCA/cosine patterns demonstrate correlates of the learned solution, not necessity or sufficiency of particular heads or neurons.

anchors.section: Section V-B, interpretation of single-anchor outputs

key_findings.claim: Reasoning-regime models correlate with neuron condensation, structured token embeddings, and lower stable rank, supporting—but not proving—a low-complexity mechanism.
key_findings.evidence: First-layer query rows align into fewer directions as gamma/weight decay rise; Phase-3 word embeddings show an ordered PCA geometry; and merged multi-head query matrices have lower stable rank in later phases. These quantities are all consequences of the same hyperparameter intervention and task success, so the evidence cannot distinguish whether low rank causes compositionality, follows it, or is an incidental effect of L2 shrinkage.

key_findings.claim: Cross-task experiments show a broad empirical regularization effect, but several are not mechanistic or genuinely real-world validations of the anchor-function explanation.
key_findings.evidence: Smaller initialization or larger weight decay improves sparse concept-graph diffusion outputs, SCAN/COGS OOD accuracy, held-range addition, SlimPajama perplexity, and PrOntoQA accuracy. Yet Concept Graphs and PrOntoQA remain synthetic; SCAN/COGS are controlled benchmarks; lower language-model perplexity is not compositional reasoning; and the paper reports selected curves without a uniform hyperparameter budget, statistical intervals, or comparisons to tuned compositional architectures.

anchors.section: SCAN, COGS, addition, SlimPajama, and PrOntoQA setups

key_findings.claim: The proposed convergence-speed diagnostic behaves as predicted on deliberately rule-violating anchor pairs, but the test is circular and limited to known synthetic partitions.
key_findings.evidence: With small initialization, training takes longer as the number of anchor-pair groups whose targets violate primitive composition increases; with large initialization it remains roughly constant. Specific affected pairs also cross 60% accuracy later. The paper defines 'reasoning complexity' directly as the number of injected violations, so this validates sensitivity to the intervention rather than an independently calibrated detector of noisy real data.

key_findings.claim: Author-acknowledged trade-off: biasing toward simple rule learning can reduce memorization capacity, and all detailed mechanism work uses small synthetic models.
key_findings.evidence: The discussion explicitly limits mechanistic analysis to synthetic data and smaller models and notes that enhanced reasoning preference can compromise recall. RAG and mixtures of experts are proposed as speculative compensators; neither is evaluated in this work.

anchors.section: Section IX, limitation and future work

key_findings.claim: Novelty audit: this manuscript is an expanded version of the authors' NeurIPS 2024 paper, not an independent first report of the initialization result.
key_findings.evidence: Section I states it extends the conference paper with refined phases, new masking, unified stable-rank analysis, weight decay, and additional image/language tasks. The arXiv record also says it was mistakenly submitted as a replacement to arXiv:2405.05409v4. The central initialization-versus-reasoning discovery, anchor benchmark, and low-complexity hypothesis were already published in that same-author paper.

anchors.section: End of Section I, extension over conference paper

method.core_idea: Treat initialization standard deviation d_in^-gamma and L2 weight decay as complexity controls, then compare memorized versus primitive-rule solutions on held-out compositions and probe their internal representations.
method.mechanism: Train GPT-2 or a two-layer single-head decoder on arithmetic anchor pairs with strictly held-out pair combinations; sweep gamma and weight decay; label empirical performance phases; mask selected attention information paths; quantify row-direction condensation, embedding geometry, and stable rank; and test the same hyperparameter direction on diffusion and language tasks.
assumptions: Held-out anchor-pair accuracy faithfully distinguishes primitive composition from pair-level lookup.
The arithmetic anchors commute, making swapped-pair agreement an informative but task-specific abstraction probe.
Smaller initialization and weight decay can be treated as a common scalar notion of model complexity despite different optimization effects.
Post-softmax masking preserves enough of the ordinary computation to interpret output geometry.
Stable rank of the first-layer query matrix and row cosine similarity meaningfully summarize functional complexity.
Hyperparameter effects found in small controlled tasks transfer to larger architectures and natural workloads.

techniques.role: Separate seen-key generalization from unseen compositions of individually seen operations.
Map regularization choices to memorization, pair abstraction, and primitive-rule regimes.
Remove key-token or second-anchor paths and compare the resulting output representations.
Measure alignment among first-layer query input-weight rows.
Summarize effective dimensionality of merged multi-head query matrices.
Relate convergence time under strong complexity control to injected departures from primitive composition.

evaluations.setting: 900,000-example arithmetic anchor corpus; ten-layer, ten-head GPT-2; 14 seen and two held-out pairs
evaluations.metric: Training, ID, held-pair OOD accuracy, swapped-pair commutativity, and stable rank
evaluations.result: Higher gamma (smaller scale) and stronger weight decay shift models toward high OOD accuracy, commutativity, and lower stable rank after ID fitting.
evaluations.baseline: Other points in the same hyperparameter grid; three seeds.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer, one-head transformer trained on the same anchor task
evaluations.metric: Masked-output PCA/cosine similarity, query-row cosine similarity, and token-embedding PCA
evaluations.result: Phase 3 organizes symmetric pairs and intermediate single-anchor values and shows condensed query rows and structured embeddings.
evaluations.baseline: Phase 1 and Phase 2 checkpoints selected through performance thresholds.

evaluations.setting: Concept Graphs conditional diffusion with sparse attribute combinations
evaluations.metric: Qualitative generated shape for held-out 010/011 concepts
evaluations.result: Decreasing initialization scale changes outputs from the previously reported wrong triangle toward the target circle.
evaluations.baseline: Default Kaiming-uniform initialization used in prior Concept Graphs work.

evaluations.setting: SCAN, COGS, held-range addition, SlimPajama GPT-2 Medium, and PrOntoQA
evaluations.metric: Task accuracy or language-model perplexity across data scale
evaluations.result: The small-initialization/large-weight-decay configurations generally outperform the opposite configurations, including COGS OOD when both have over 99% ID accuracy.
evaluations.baseline: Paired regularization settings, not architecture-specialized or comprehensively tuned state of the art.

evaluations.setting: 100,000-example anchor datasets with 0-6 deliberately noncompositional symmetric pair groups, nine trials
evaluations.metric: Epochs to low loss/100% accuracy and per-pair epochs to 60% accuracy
evaluations.result: Small-initialization models slow as violations increase and specifically slow on affected pairs; large-initialization models are comparatively insensitive.
evaluations.baseline: Different initialization scales on a synthetic intervention where complexity is defined by the injected violations.

limitations: Author-acknowledged: internal mechanism analysis is confined to synthetic data and smaller models.
Author-acknowledged: a stronger reasoning bias can sacrifice memorization that some tasks require.
Reviewer-identified: the study is empirical and offers no theorem that initialization, weight decay, condensation, or low stable rank causes rule learning.
Reviewer-identified: phase boundaries depend on arbitrary accuracy and commutativity thresholds and may change with training horizon or tuning.
Reviewer-identified: weight decay mechanically reduces norms and can alter effective learning rates, so grouping it with initialization as a single 'complexity' intervention is underidentified.
Reviewer-identified: PCA, stable rank, and masked-output similarity are correlated probes, not causal circuit localization.
Reviewer-identified: the core anchor task uses commuting affine operations and a narrow holdout, so alternate algorithms or dataset shortcuts may produce identical OOD behavior.
Reviewer-identified: cross-task comparisons do not consistently report uncertainty, equal compute, complete hyperparameter search, or tuned baselines.
Reviewer-identified: calling SlimPajama perplexity and synthetic Concept Graphs 'real-world' reasoning validation overstates ecological coverage.
Reviewer-identified: the paper is explicitly an extension of the same authors' NeurIPS 2024 publication.
failure_modes: Too-small initialization can slow optimization, suppress useful feature diversity, or fall outside the purported reasoning basin.
Strong weight decay can cause underfitting or erase facts whose correct solution genuinely requires memorization.
An OOD split can accidentally reward commutativity or token arithmetic without testing broader systematic composition.
Post-softmax masking can create activations never encountered in training and yield misleading geometry.
Low stable rank can arise from regularization without representing a correct algorithm.
Hyperparameters that help from-scratch training may be destructive during pretrained-model fine-tuning.
Training speed can flag rare or hard examples rather than true rule violations.
reusable_insights: Use held-out combinations of individually observed primitives to distinguish interpolation from systematic composition.
Treat initialization and regularization as algorithm-selection knobs, not merely training-stability defaults.
Require multiple mechanistic probes to agree, but follow correlational geometry with causal ablation and reconstitution tests.
Explicitly measure the reasoning-memory Pareto frontier; a single strongest-regularization setting is unlikely to dominate mixed workloads.
Training-window interventions can test whether a static regularizer shapes early representation selection or merely compresses the final solution.
When claiming broad transfer, separate controlled benchmarks, natural corpora, and deployed task distributions.
open_questions: At what training stage does initialization or weight decay commit a model to a memorization versus reasoning basin?
Can matched norm, effective-step-size, and spectral interventions isolate condensation from generic L2 effects?
Does selectively regularizing attention, embeddings, MLPs, or experts preserve factual memory while promoting primitive composition?
Which causal circuits are necessary and sufficient for the intermediate g(x;a1) representation?
How robust is the phase diagram to noncommutative operations, longer compositions, noisy primitives, and ambiguous algorithms?
Do pretrained frontier-scale models exhibit the same initialization dependence, or has pretraining already fixed their basin?
Can online rank or activation diagnostics select regularization schedules without access to held-out OOD compositions?

competitive_landscape.title: Initialization is Critical to Whether Transformers Fit Composite Functions by Reasoning or Memorizing
competitive_landscape.difference: This NeurIPS 2024 paper already contains the central anchor benchmark, initialization-controlled memory/reasoning distinction, internal representation analysis, and low-complexity hypothesis. The reviewed manuscript adds weight decay, refined phases and masking, stable rank, more tasks, and convergence diagnostics; its novelty is the extension, not the headline result.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Capabilities of Autoregressive Transformers: A Study on Synthetic, Interpretable Tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: Ramesh et al. systematically vary data and model factors on interpretable compositions and document generalization limits. Zhang et al. focus on optimizer-induced solution selection and propose initialization/weight decay as a way to move between lookup and primitive-rule mechanisms.

competitive_landscape.title: Making Transformers Solve Compositional Tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: Csordas et al. show that architectural and optimization design choices can greatly improve systematic generalization across COGS and PCFG. The reviewed work isolates initialization scale and weight decay and supplies representation probes, but does not compare against that broader tuned design space.

competitive_landscape.title: A Minimal Model for Compositional Generalization on gSCAN
competitive_landscape.difference: This work already reports that weight decay and attention facilitate compositional generalization by inducing sparse, context-invariant representations in a minimal model. Zhang et al. broaden the observation to Transformer/diffusion tasks and tie it to initialization, condensation, and stable rank.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokked Transformers are Implicit Reasoners: A Mechanistic Journey to the Edge of Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. connect delayed generalization in modular reasoning to interpretable internal algorithms and memorization-to-reasoning transitions over training. Zhang et al. emphasize static initialization/weight-decay selection across held-out compositions rather than temporal grokking, though both associate generalization with simpler structure.

competitive_landscape.title: Critical Windows of Complexity Control: When Transformers Decide to Reason or Memorize
competitive_landscape.difference: Ali temporally localizes the weight-decay effect and reports that a narrow middle window can match full-training regularization; it also finds the reasoning basin can shrink at small initialization, contradicting a uniform 'smaller is better' recommendation. This turns the reviewed static phase diagram into a schedule- and stage-dependent hypothesis.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Complexity control through initialization and weight decay determines whether Transformers memorize composite mappings or learn primitive rules, with distinct masked circuits and low-rank/condensed structure that generalizes across image and language tasks.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Hyperparameter phase sweeps, two masking probes, condensation/embedding/stable-rank analyses, five cross-task families, and a rule-violation convergence intervention all move in the predicted direction.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The expanded empirical synthesis is useful, especially connecting weight decay, stable rank, cross-domain tests, and convergence diagnostics. However, the main discovery was already published by the same authors at NeurIPS 2024, causal claims exceed the correlational probes, and a later direct stress test shows the preferred initialization is training-window dependent. Treat this record as an extended companion paper and hypothesis generator, not independent confirmation or a general theory of reasoning.

reviewer_notes: All 16 extracted pages were read, including experimental appendices. Primary competing sources were checked on official NeurIPS, OpenReview, and arXiv pages on 2026-08-23. The arXiv metadata's mistaken-replacement note and the manuscript's explicit extension statement were included in the novelty audit.
